paper_name: Workload assignment for global real-time scheduling on unrelated multicore platforms
paper_description: Extends global scheduling to unrelated multicore platforms (clusters), providing optimal polynomial-time workload assignments minimizing migrations, with simulation showing benefits over related models.

formal_description.statement: Platform with clusters C_l of m_l unrelated speed processors; task tau_i execution C_i_l on cluster l varies by speed factor s_l.

informal_sketch.intuition: Clusters as unrelated units for migration limits.

formal_description.statement: Workload assignment poly-time optimal: assign fractions f_i_l to clusters s.t. sum f_i_l =1, U_i * sum f_i_l / s_l <=1, min migrations.
formal_description.conclusion: Schedulable if max load <=1 per cluster

steps: LP: min sum migrations s.t. loads <=1
